text:
The Maple Leafs finally won on Sunday, 4-2 on Long Island after falling two goals behind, and it ended a nine-game winless run (0-8-1). One win doesn't quiet much in Toronto. Auston Matthews has been in 30 headlines in two weeks, most of them about his future, with Elliotte Friedman quoted as saying "All bets are off." William Nylander has been in just as many, after Jim Hiller called out his mistakes during the skid, and The Leafs Nation reports he has been dropped to the second power-play unit for tonight. Our playoff simulations give Toronto a 3% chance, with 21 points from games whose chances were worth 25.1.

Boston looks steadier from a distance, but its own week has wobbled: four losses in five home games for the first time since December 2016, as Ty Anderson of 98.5 The Sports Hub pointed out. The Bruins are +19 in goal difference on chances worth about +2, which is a long way of saying finishing and Jeremy Swayman (9.7 goals saved above expected as a team, 6.1 of them his) have done a lot of the lifting. Swayman's last few starts have drawn worried headlines, and he was worth 26.5 goals above expected last season, so the bar is high.

Elias Lindholm is the hot hand, 11 points in his last 10 games including four goals against Washington, and he is centering Marat Khusnutdinov, our depth sleeper, who has moved into James Hagens' spot. We have Khusnutdinov at 17% to score.

Toronto is still without Jack Roslovic (23 points in 24 games) and, in our numbers, Kirill Marchenko, though TSN's Thursday headline had Marchenko talking about a return. If he dresses, that's 14 points in 14 games our projection doesn't include. As it stands our numbers give Boston 3.57 expected goals to Toronto's 2.54, and Matthews 39% to score, riding a four-game point streak into a building where the questions about him will follow.
headline: The Leafs bring their questions to Boston
